summary: CLAIM C-0003: The labor force was a large, well-fed, rotating body of Egyptian workers (corvée / paid), not slaves; the exact size is contested but the 'slave labor' narrative is rejected.
content: The 'slaves built the pyramids' idea is rejected by archaeologists; the builders were Egyptian workers organized into gangs/phyles/divisions, fed well (beef, bread, beer) and housed in a workers' town (EV-0012, EV-0015). Labor size estimates range widely: Herodotus ~100,000 (EV-0013), Lehner ~5,000 local builders plus others (EV-0013), DMJM average ~14,567 / peak ~40,000 (EV-0014). Consensus on 'not slaves'; exact number contested.
